texts.preamble: Dharanikota Veeranji, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 25 January, 2021 In The High Court Of Andhra Pradesh At Amaravati x Monday, The Twenty Fifth Day Of January Two Thousand And Twenty One :Present: The Honourable Smt Justice Lalitha Kanneganti Criminal Petition No: 307 Of 2021 Between: 1. Dharanikota Veeranji, S/o. Anjaneyulu, Hindu, aged about 25 years, R/o. Patimeeda Bazaar, Vinukonda Town, Guntur District. 2. Anakapalli Anji Reddy @ Somu, S/o. Pedda Venkatareddy, Hindu, aged about years, R/o. Gangavaram Village, Thalluru Mandal, Prakasam District. 3. Thota Venkaiah, S/o. Peda Ramaiah, Hindu, aged about 65 years, R/o. Bharathapuram Village, Vinukonda Mandal, Guntur District. ... Petitioners/Accused And The State of Andhra Pradesh, Rep. by its Public Prosecutor, High Court Buildings, Amaravathi. ... Respondent/Complainant Petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C, praying that in the circumstances stated in the memorandum of grounds filed in Criminal Petition, the High Court may be pleased to quash the proceedings in Fir No. 5 Of 2021, dated 04-01-2021 on the file of Vinukonda Town Police Station, Guntur District. Ia No: 2 Of 2021 Petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C praying that in the circumstances stated in the memorandum of grounds filed in Criminal Petition, the High Court may be pleased to stay all further proceedings in Fir No. 5 Of 2021, Dated 04-01-2021 on the file of Vinukonda town Police Station, Guntur District, pending disposal of Crlp 307 of 2021, on the file of the High Court. The petition coming on for hearing, upon perusing the Petition and the memorandum of grounds filed in support thereof and upon hearing the arguments of Sri Raja Reddy Koneti, Advocate for the Petitioners and of Public Prosecutor for the Respondent, the Court made the following. Order
texts.facts: The petitioners before this Court are Al to A3 in the above said crime. 3. The brief facts of the case are that while the Police were on duty on 04.01.2021 at about 5:00 P.M. they found one person i.e. petitioner No.1 at the house of petitioner No.3, who tried to run away on seeing the Police. But he was apprehended by the Police and on questioning petitioner No.1 confessed that he purchased the said gutka and khaini packets from petitioner No.2 and that the said stock was kept in the house of petitioner No.3. Basing on the same the present crime is registered against the petitioners and the tobacco products were seized. 4.
texts.arguments: 5. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that Sections 272 and 273 I.P.C. relate to food safety standards. Section 272 I.P.C. speaks about adulteration of food or drink intended for sale =x thoy . . and Section 273 of I.P.C. speaks about sale of Noxious Food or Drink. He further submits that possession, sale, purchase and transport of banned gutka and tobacco products will not attract the offences as alleged as they do not fall under the definition of food and also do not, spread any disease. Moreover, the Police have no power to register the offences under above Sections except the designated officers like Food Safety Officer. Further Section 188 I.P.C. would apply when there is disobedience of an order duly promulgated by a public servant. As such even Section 188 I.P.C. is not applicable to the present case. 7. Learned Counsel for the petitioners placed reliance on the common order dated 18.12.2019 passed by a coordinate Bench of this Court in Criminal Petition Nos.5421 of 2019 and batch, wherein FIRs which were registered under similar circumstances were [LEAKAGE_MASK] holding that tobacco does not fall within the definition of "food" as specified under Section 3(i)(j) of the FSS Act and therefore, registration of FIR under the above sections is not permissible.
